title: This Frog Buries Itself in Desert Dirt for Years, Wrapped in Its Own Skin
subject: water-holding frog

scenes.text: This frog waits years in the desert without a drop of water. How?
The water-holding frog lives in Australia, where rain can skip years.
When the ground dries, it digs down and swells up with stored water.
Then it sheds layer after layer of skin and wraps itself in a waterproof cocoon.
It can stay buried up to five years. People crossing the desert even dug them up to drink.
Then summer rain soaks in, the frog wakes, and it climbs out to feed and breed.

description:
The water-holding frog of Australia can stay buried for up to five years, sealed in a cocoon made of its own shed skin.
It stores water in its body and wakes when heavy summer rain soaks the ground.
Could you wait that long?
first_comment: Which animal would win a desert survival contest? This frog stores water in its body and seals itself in skin.
